title: Net worth — how to measure your money progress
publisher: Artha Kavach summary of public guidance (RBI / SEBI / IRDAI / Income Tax Dept) — pending manual verification
text: Net worth is everything you own (savings, investments, PF, gold, property value) minus everything you owe (loans, card dues). It is a better measure of progress than income because it shows whether you are actually building wealth. List assets and liabilities once, update every three or six months, and watch the trend rather than the exact number. A young person starting out with a negative net worth (because of an education loan) is normal; what matters is that it rises. Exclude things that lose value fast, such as the resale value of a phone, unless you plan to sell them. Pair it with your savings rate: if you save 20% of income and invest it regularly, net worth will usually follow.
summary_hinglish: Net worth = jo tumhare paas hai (savings, investments, PF, gold, property) minus jo tumhe dena hai (loans, card dues). Income se behtar progress ka measure hai. Har 3-6 mahine mein update karo aur trend dekho. Education loan ki wajah se shuru mein negative hona normal hai, badhna zaroori hai.
summary_hi: नेट वर्थ = जो आपके पास है (बचत, निवेश, PF, सोना, संपत्ति) माइनस जो आपको चुकाना है (लोन, कार्ड बकाया)। यह आय से बेहतर प्रगति का माप है। हर 3-6 महीने में अपडेट करें और रुझान देखें। शुरू में एजुकेशन लोन की वजह से नेगेटिव होना सामान्य है, बढ़ना ज़रूरी है।
